correctness_confidence.basis: Core identities and asymptotics in Theorems 2.1, 2.3, 3.1, 4.1, and 5.1(a) check out under independent derivation, including the O(c2*s^-2) cancellation and h^(4) = 6*c2*alpha1*(alpha1+1)/s1^6 matching; minor technical gaps appear in Theorem 5.1(b) and Theorem 4.1's log_Q^ub details, and external Lean/Python artifacts were not executed.

novelty.basis: The exact covariance-boundary law (Thm 2.1), two-order O(tau^-2) bias cancellation in the shift-invariant cumulant pair (Thm 2.3), and the cumulant-matched Le Cam two-point construction (Thm 5.1(a)) are genuine original contributions; Thms 3.1 and 4.1 adapt classical asymptotics and Stieltjes-Hankel moment theory.

reproducibility.basis: Explicit benchmark models, parameter values, and a symbol-level Lean 4 manifest (Table 1) are documented in the manuscript; however, this review inspected only main.pdf and did not run the referenced repository scripts or Lean kernel.

rigor.basis: Analytical proofs of Theorems 2.1, 2.3, 3.1, 4.1, and 5.1(a) are well-structured with explicit assumptions; Theorem 5.1(b) omits clipping/truncation needed to prevent undefined log(F_hat) or division by zero under Gaussian noise and uses an oracle tau*(sigma) depending on unknown Delta.

significance.basis: Substantially improves finite-tau continuum-edge estimation over [6] and clarifies information-theoretic limits under additive noise, though practical utility of Delta_hat_SI is limited to high SNR (sigma <= 10^-6) or deterministic simulations and Hankel bounds certify only upper limits.

potential_errors: Unclipped Gaussian noise in Theorem 5.1(b) creates a tiny nonzero-probability event where F_hat <= 0.
Eq. (11) writes strict '>' for geometric tail enclosure of log((1+t)/(1-t)) which is equality at t=0.
strengths: Theorem 2.1 establishes a clean, exact non-asymptotic identity for Delta_hat_VF(tau) - Delta.
Theorem 2.3(b) identifies exact O(c2*s^-2) cancellation jumping directly to O(tau^-3) bias.
Theorem 5.1(a) yields matching poly-logarithmic Le Cam minimax lower bounds.
Section 6 and Table 1 transparently scope the 16 Lean 4 core algebraic lemmas.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact covariance-boundary representation for Delta_hat_VF(tau) - Delta (Theorem 2.1).
Shift-invariant cumulant estimators with exact O(c2*s^-2) cancellation (Theorem 2.3).
Asymptotic-window Le Cam minimax lower bounds via fourth-order cumulant matching (Theorem 5.1(a)).
summary: The manuscript addresses finite-imaginary-time bias, assumption-free certification, and additive-noise resolution limits when extracting continuum spectral gaps Delta and threshold exponents alpha from imaginary-time evolution decay functions F(tau). The main mathematical claims are sound, with several minor technical and expositional issues requiring clarification.
weaknesses: In Theorem 5.1(b), unclipped Gaussian noise needs truncation/regularization event for strict RMSE finiteness.
Abstract wording on 1D/3D gains omits that 3D gain in Table 2 is 142x.
